questions.stem: Two angles on a straight line are $x$ and $135°$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line sum to $180°$, so $x = 180° - 135° = 45°$.

questions.stem: Four angles meet at a point. Three of them are $90°$, $85°$, and $110°$. What is the fourth angle?
questions.explanation: Angles at a point sum to $360°$. The fourth angle is $360° - 90° - 85° - 110° = 75°$.

questions.stem: Two straight lines intersect. One of the angles formed is $72°$. What is the vertically opposite angle?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the angle is $72°$.

questions.stem: Three angles on a straight line are $x$, $2x$, and $3x$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line sum to $180°$: $x + 2x + 3x = 6x = 180°$, so $x = 30°$.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One angle is $(3x + 10)°$ and the vertically opposite angle is $70°$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal: $3x + 10 = 70$, so $3x = 60$ and $x = 20$.

questions.stem: An angle measuring $150°$ is classified as:
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is between $90°$ and $180°$. Since $150°$ falls in this range, it is obtuse.

questions.stem: Two lines intersect. One angle is $y$ and the adjacent angle is $(2y + 30)°$. What is the value of $y$?
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to $180°$: $y + 2y + 30 = 180$, so $3y = 150$ and $y = 50°$.
